==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alt|en|idjit|idget||nonstandard|indicating the pronunciation /ˈɪd͡ʒət/}}
* {{alt|en|eejit||Irish|Scottish|nonstandard}}

===Etymology===
{{ety|en|:inh|enm:ydiote|tree=1}}
From {{inh|en|enm|idiote}}, {{m|enm|ydiote}}, from {{der|en|fro|idiote}} (later {{m|fro|idiot}}), from {{der|en|la|idiota}}, from {{der|en|grc|ἰδιώτης||a private citizen, one who has no professional knowledge, layman}}, from {{m|grc|ἴδιος||one's own, pertaining to oneself, private}}. {{doublet|en|idiota}}. {{surf|en|idi-|-ot}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|ĭdĭət||a=UK,US}}, {{IPA|en|/ˈɪdiət/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɪd͡ʒət/|a=yod-coalescence,non-standard}}
* {{audio|en|En-us-idiot.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|id|i|ot}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# {{senseid|en|Q193607}} {{lb|en|pejorative}} A person of low general [[intelligence]].
#: {{syn|en|imbecile<id:Q193607>|moron<id:Q193607>|retard<id:Q193607><qq:offensive>|Thesaurus:fool|Thesaurus:idiot}}
#: {{ux|en|Only an '''idiot''' would fail this exam.}}
#: {{ux|en| After failing a hat-trick of exams, the teacher called him an '''idiot'''.}}
# {{lb|en|pejorative}} A person who makes stupid decisions; a [[fool]].
#: {{ux|en| He thought people who don't like cricket are '''idiots'''. He later got into fights with people who like football.}}
#: {{ux|en|We think that people who cycle without a helmet are '''idiots'''.}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Devan Cole|title=Biden calls Trump an ‘idiot’ for dismissing Russian election interference|url=https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/28/politics/joe-biden-donald-trump-idiot|date=2019-10-28|passage=“He’s an '''idiot''' – in terms of saying that. Everybody knows this. Everybody knows it. Nobody doubts it,” Biden said.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240408183851/https://www.cnn.com/2019/10/28/politics/joe-biden-donald-trump-idiot/|archivedate=8 April 2024}}
#* {{RQ:en:CNN|author=Andrew Kaczynski|title=RFK Jr. compared Trump to Hitler and praised descriptions of his supporters as ‘Nazis’|url=https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/21/politics/kfile-rfk-jr-trump-critique|date=2024-11-21|passage=“One of the things that you write so beautifully, and your stuff is so fun to read, but you write about Trump, quote, ‘The way that you build a truly vicious nationalist movement is to wed a relatively small core of belligerent '''idiots''' to a much larger group of opportunists and spineless fellow travelers whose primary function is to turn a blind eye to things,’” Kennedy said, reading Taibbi’s own writing back to him.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20260329163824/https://www.cnn.com/2024/11/21/politics/kfile-rfk-jr-trump-critique|archivedate=29 March 2026}}
# {{senseid|en|person with Q183560}} {{lb|en|obsolete|medicine|psychology}} A person of the lowest intellectual standing, a person who lacks the capacity to develop beyond the mental age of a normal four-year-old; a person with an [[IQ]] below 30.
#: {{syn|en|imbecile<id:person with Q183560>|moron<id:person with Q183560>|retard<id:person with Q183560><qq:offensive>}}
#* {{quote-book |en |author={{w|Clifton Johnson (author)|Clifton Johnson}} |page=105 |chapter=[[:s:en:What They Say in New England/Folks|Folks]] |title=[[:s:en:What They Say in New England|What They Say in New England]] |text='''Idiots''' were thought to be peculiarly under the care of the Deity, and it was believed that those who treated them kindly would be blessed. |year=1896 |publisher=Lee and Shepard Publishers |location=Boston, Massachusetts, United States |genre=non-fiction}}

====Usage notes====
* While pejorative, the word is only a weak insult, and between close friends or family members it may be used affectionately.
